item.title: Ars Biologica ArtXScience Residency 2027-2028 (Ars Electronica x Ceske Budejovice ECoC 2028)
item.description:
Organisation: Ars Electronica and Ceske Budejovice - European Capital of Culture 2028

Location: Ceske Budejovice, Czech Republic. Open to applicants of any nationality aged 18+ who are legally eligible to work and travel in the EU. Required on-site stays: up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and March 2028 for installation, exhibition and deinstallation.

Award: EUR 24,000 total package per winner: EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production budget, and up to EUR 3,000 for travel, accommodation and subsistence, plus a separate budget covering one month of housing in Ceske Budejovice. Two positions available. Free to apply.

Duration: January 2027 to April 2028, with on-site blocks in early 2027 and March 2028

Deadline: 28 Sep 2026

A fully funded art-science residency from Ars Electronica and Ceske Budejovice, European Capital of Culture 2028, exploring how art and science can collaborate on urgent environmental challenges: climate emergence, sustainable agriculture, geoengineering, permaculture, water resource management, and the broader ecological impacts on local communities. Selected residents work in direct collaboration with local scientists in Ceske Budejovice. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, designers, creatives and artist collectives with more than 5 years of professional creative practice and documented interdisciplinary work; experience in community engagement and science collaborations is essential; applicants must be 18+, of any nationality, and legally eligible to work and travel in the EU. WHAT YOU GET: a EUR 24,000 package (EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production, up to EUR 3,000 travel and subsistence) plus one month of housing covered separately; two winners are selected. STRUCTURE: the residency runs January 2027 to April 2028, with a required on-site stay of up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and a March 2028 stay for festival installation, exhibition and deinstallation. HOW TO APPLY: online form with project title, a written proposal of max 250 words, a scientific direction statement (max 100 words), artistic vision (max 100 words), community connection plan (max 100 words), a super short pitch (3 to 30 words), 3 to 7 images, an optional 1-minute video, a portfolio link and contact information. Two-round selection (online application then interview); winners notified by November 2026. Deadline 28 September 2026 at midnight CET.

item.title: Video Pool: Media Art + Technology Residency (MATR) 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Video Pool Media Arts Centre

Location: In person at Video Pool Media Arts Centre and its Poolside Gallery, 221-100 Arthur Street, Winnipeg, Manitoba R3B 1H3, Canada.

Award: CAD 2,250 artist fee, covering both the residency period and the subsequent Poolside Gallery exhibition. Residents also get full access to VP's equipment, facilities and technical resources; the Poolside Gallery itself is equipped with two projectors and four speakers. Applicants must be VP members, so a membership is purchased separately, but there is no separate application fee.

Duration: Up to two months to develop and install the project, including one month of dedicated access to the Poolside Gallery. Residency takes place in Winter 2027; exhibition dates TBD.

Deadline: 30 Aug 2026

Video Pool's Media Art + Technology Residency supports experimental, independent, technology-based work. The selected artist or artists develop a new project (or adapt and transform an existing one) in direct response to the intimate scale and specific character of the Poolside Gallery, culminating in an exhibition there. The call is deliberately open on medium: video, sound, installation, digital media, performance, interactive technologies, expanded cinema and interdisciplinary practices are all welcome. VP asks proposals to speak clearly to your practice, the questions, materials or ideas that drive the work, and how that work might grow, shift or take new form inside the gallery. It is explicitly interested in expansive proposals, work that pushes past the gallery's four walls to engage its surrounding spaces (hallways, windows, projection wall) or that reimagines what the gallery itself can hold, and in projects that engage technology as a creative, critical, aesthetic or socio-political tool. Priority is given to artists from equity-seeking communities whose practices contribute to the advancement of experimental media arts. Residents get full access to VP's available equipment, facilities and technical resources throughout the residency, and applicants are encouraged to review the equipment and facilities list before proposing. ELIGIBILITY: open to VP members (this is a member submission call); no nationality restriction is stated, but the residency and exhibition are in person in Winnipeg. APPLICATION: artist bio (1,500 characters), headshot, description of your artistic practice (3,000 characters), project proposal for MATR (3,000 characters), equipment and facility needs (750 characters), description of how you would use the space (750 characters), CV, up to five images (optional) and up to two video or documentation links. Submit via the online form at videopool.org/matr-2027-application/ by 30 August 2026; alternative submission formats can be arranged by contacting Emma (emma@videopool.org) or Iyunade (iyunade@videopool.org). General enquiries: info@videopool.org, 204-949-9134.

item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Residency Videotage 2027 (Hong Kong)
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL) in collaboration with Videotage, Hong Kong

Location: Residency takes place at Videotage in Hong Kong. Applicants must be established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands) and registered in a business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Award: EUR 5,000 for a two-month residency or EUR 6,500 for a three-month residency, paid by the Creative Industries Fund NL to cover travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested, and material and transport costs. Accommodation, use of the studio space and facilitation by Videotage are covered directly by the Fund on top of this. No application fee.

Duration: Two or three months in 2027 (spring 2027); state your preferred period in the application.

Deadline: 21 Oct 2026

The Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) runs this residency with Videotage, a Hong Kong-based non-profit media arts institution specialising in the promotion, presentation, creation and preservation of moving image and media art in all forms and languages. The Fund is recruiting one Netherlands-based designer, maker or observer working in digital culture to spend two or three months at Videotage's studio space in Hong Kong in 2027, conducting research, broadening their network, developing new work inspired by Hong Kong, and presenting their findings or completed works. The residency encourages crossovers and experimentation, giving the participant space to explore new methodologies, widen their creative practice and produce work that pushes the boundaries of digital culture, with a focus on social and urban dynamics. The 2027 edition takes the technological 'black box' phenomenon as its starting point and invites the resident to respond to that theme within the context of Videotage. ELIGIBILITY: you are an individual designer, maker or observer within the field of digital culture; you are established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands); you are registered in the business register of the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) or another business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; and you have had a professional practice in the creative industry for at least four years. NOT open to duos, collectives or cooperative ventures, nor to designers and makers who receive a grant during the work period under the Talent Development Grant Scheme, the Open Call Self-taught Designer or the Open Call Emerging Design Practices ABCSSS. Note that accepting this open call means you cannot apply to those schemes and open calls in 2027. FUNDING: EUR 5,000 for two months or EUR 6,500 for three months, covering travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested and material and transport costs; accommodation, studio use and Videotage's facilitation are covered separately by the Fund. Submit your proposal to the Creative Industries Fund NL by 21 October 2026, 16:00 CEST.

item.title: Martin Roth-Initiative: Temporary Relocation for Artists and Cultural Actors at Risk (Programme Line 1, 2026 call)
item.description:
Organisation: Martin Roth-Initiative (Goethe-Institut and ifa, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office)

Location: Germany (relocation to a German host organisation). Open to artists and cultural actors worldwide, with exclusions.

Award: Monthly scholarship for the relocated artist, plus insurance, language courses, psychosocial support, counselling and training, visa support, and personnel funding for the host organisation. No application fee.

Duration: Up to 15 months, starting no earlier than 15 January 2027

Deadline: 11 Sep 2026

The Martin Roth-Initiative is the German temporary-relocation programme for artists and cultural actors at risk, run jointly by the Goethe-Institut and ifa with Federal Foreign Office funding. Programme Line 1 relocates an artist to Germany for up to 15 months on a scholarship, with insurance, language courses, psychosocial support, counselling and visa assistance, plus personnel funding for the hosting organisation. ELIGIBILITY: artists and cultural practitioners anywhere in the world who are demonstrably committed through their work to an open society, freedom, peace and democracy; who face threats, persecution or unsafe living conditions; who have no access to a safe place to continue working; and who speak English or German. Applicants must still be active in their home country or have left it after 20 February 2026. Citizens of EU and EEA countries, Australia, Canada, Israel, New Zealand, Switzerland, the UK and the USA are excluded, as are residents of Gaza and previous MRI recipients. HOST REQUIREMENT: applications are submitted jointly with a non-profit host organisation in Germany (museum, theatre, festival, cultural collective, NGO) that is a legal entity able to handle the administrative and digital-security requirements. Note that the scholarship visa does not itself permit employment or self-employment in Germany. TIMELINE: applications 6 July to 11 September 2026; decisions end of November 2026; funding starts no earlier than 15 January 2027. Apply to apply@mri-application.de (encrypted email recommended); phone +49 30 284491-77.

item.title: UAL AKO Storytelling Institute: Storytelling Research Fellows 2026 (six posts)
item.description:
Organisation: University of the Arts London (UAL AKO Storytelling Institute), with the Power of Pop Fund

Location: High Holborn, London, United Kingdom (hybrid)

Award: GBP 48,563 per annum pro rata (around GBP 19,425 for the part-time fellowship hours), plus UAL benefits. No application fee.

Duration: Nine-month fellowship, part-time, culminating in a public symposium

Deadline: 11 Sep 2026

The UAL AKO Storytelling Institute, with the Power of Pop Fund, is recruiting six Storytelling Research Fellows to run independent research projects on how storytelling in popular culture shapes attitudes, behaviour and public discourse. Fellows work across media including television, film, gaming, podcasts and digital culture, are supported by the Institute's Head of Research and a peer cohort, and produce actionable findings for creative practitioners, funders and social-impact organisations, presented at a closing public symposium. ELIGIBILITY: experienced researchers with a PhD or equivalent research expertise gained academically, independently or through professional practice, with a track record of delivering high-quality research and working with external partners. Practice-based and non-academic researchers are explicitly in scope. APPLICATION: CV, record of publications, a research proposal of 1,000 to 1,200 words, and a supporting statement including at least one example of a research project you designed and delivered. Applications via the UAL jobs portal; closes 11 September 2026.

item.title: Aspen Global Change Institute: Climate and Environment Data Stewardship Fellow
item.description:
Organisation: Aspen Global Change Institute (AGCI), with Public Environmental Data Partners

Location: Remote anywhere within the continental United States. AGCI's primary office is in Basalt, Colorado, under an 'Institute Without Walls' approach. Travel: up to 8 domestic trips a year and up to 1 international trip.

Award: Anticipated salary USD 85,000 to 100,000, based on the general US market.

Duration: Full-time for 1 year; start as soon as possible and no later than 1 October 2026

Deadline: Closed 19 Aug 2026

AGCI is hiring a Climate and Environment Data Stewardship Fellow to coordinate and contribute to cross-organizational climate and environmental data stewardship efforts, supporting synergies and collective learning across established initiatives and networks focused on the collection and management of data used to inform climate action, in ways that promote long-term data quality, accessibility, interoperability and security. PLACEMENT AND MENTORSHIP: the fellow sits within AGCI's Engaged Research Team, reporting to AGCI's Research Director, with day-to-day mentorship from leaders at core partner organisations in the data stewardship space, including the Data Foundation (Sonia Wang) and Public Environmental Data Partners' co-founding member the Open Environmental Data Project (Brittany Janis), plus guidance from other leaders in the field. RESPONSIBILITIES: coordination of the coordinators, using a network-of-networks approach to build connectedness across emerging and existing work in the climate and environmental data landscape and to help the network identify and act on shared priorities; planning and coordinating network meetings, workshops and other convenings, starting with consolidating the landscape analysis exercises already underway; elevating data stewardship work by developing and sharing a comprehensive picture of what is needed to sustain data critical to climate action; supporting peer learning through surveys, focus groups or scenario planning that enable cross-organisation conversations about possible futures; connecting evolving data stewardship to the broader climate action and investment ecosystem; and contributing to the Climate Reserve, including professional development programming alongside other Climate Reserve-supported fellows. REQUIREMENTS: bachelor's degree required, master's or doctorate preferred; minimum 3 years managing communities of practice (working groups, interagency groups and similar) or coordinating multi-organisation or network-based initiatives, ideally related to climate or environmental science or policy; familiarity with data stewardship principles (long-term data quality, accessibility, interoperability, security) sufficient to support conversations across technical and non-technical partners; public speaking experience; experience working across institutional, sectoral and geographic contexts at the science-policy interface; strong project management, research, analysis and synthesis skills; and willingness to travel domestically and internationally. Domain expertise in any one data stewardship area is not required, and knowledge of the civil society data stewardship space is desirable rather than expected. TERM AND PAY: full-time for one year at an anticipated USD 85,000 to 100,000. DEADLINE: priority deadline 19 August 2026. HOW TO APPLY: through the AGCI Workable posting.

item.title: Studio ALTA Residence 2027: four residency open calls (Prague)
item.description:
Organisation: Studio ALTA

Location: Studio ALTA, Prague (Liben district), Czech Republic. Three of the four calls are open internationally; the Rest House call is reserved for supporting-profession arts workers active in the Czech independent sector.

Award: Residency fees paid to participants: Research House CZK 12,000 per project; Rest House CZK 6,000 per person; House in the Neighborhood CZK 30,000 per project; House of Sweat CZK 15,000 per project. All include workspace at Studio ALTA; the two production residencies add dramaturgic, production, technical and PR support. Free to apply.

Duration: Programme dependent: 5 to 10 days, at various points between February and November 2027

Deadline: 10 Sep 2026

Prague performance venue Studio ALTA announces four residency open calls for 2027, all with a single deadline of 10 September 2026. RESEARCH HOUSE (19 to 28 April 2027): a shared residential laboratory for three art projects or individual artists in the early stages of exploration and experimentation, or reopening an existing finished work (performance, installation, object, video) to transform it into another form such as a workshop, text or performance-lecture. Includes a 10-day residency, a fee of CZK 12,000 per project, shared studio, individual workspace and facilitated exchange meetings; the research output must be shared publicly as a work-in-progress in a form based on participants' needs. REST HOUSE (March to November 2027): a five-day residential spa for overloaded colleagues from the arts sector, with no required output or activities; restricted to people working in production, dramaturgy, curation, PR, technical and other supporting artistic professions in the Czech independent sector. Two guests are chosen by lottery (fee CZK 6,000 per person); the public draw is announced 16 September 2026. HOUSE IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD (9 to 18 August 2027): for one performative art project created with the local community and designed or adapted for public space in Liben and its surroundings; this year's call focuses on the 55+ target group. Includes a fee of CZK 30,000 per project, rehearsal and indoor facilities (primarily outdoor spaces), dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, connections to partner organisations, and 7 days of intensive production and technical support in the final phase. A public premiere or work-in-progress in public space at the end of the residency is required. HOUSE OF SWEAT (1 to 10 February 2027): for one performative art project designed or adapted for the specific environment of the Studio ALTA sauna and its immediate surroundings, seeking new ways of working with intimate space, proximity to the audience and non-traditional formats. Includes a fee of CZK 15,000 per project, a 10-day residency, sauna and rehearsal spaces, dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, and 2 days of intensive final-phase support; a public work-in-progress or premiere in the sauna within the 9 to 12 February 2027 programme block is required. Projects at any stage of development can apply to the production calls, and selected projects may be included in Studio ALTA's year-round programme. TIMELINE: deadline 10 September 2026; results 3 weeks after the deadline (30 September 2026); a Q&A Zoom call takes place 10 August 2026 at 3:00 PM. Apply via the registration forms on the call page.

item.title: Helpmann Fellowships 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Helpmann Academy

Location: South Australia (applicant must be a current South Australian resident); funded activity may take place anywhere.

Award: Up to AUD 7,500 per fellowship, three fellowships available. Supported by the James & Diana Ramsay Foundation. No application fee.

Duration: Funded activity must occur between 1 January 2027 and 31 December 2027

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Three Helpmann Fellowships of up to AUD 7,500 support ambitious, self-directed projects that advance the artistic and professional development of emerging creatives. Fellowships are open across all eligible disciplines, to individuals and to collectives, and funding can go to larger-scale creative projects, tailored professional development, or a combination of both. Previous fellowships have supported the creation of new work, exhibitions and performances, residencies and internships, touring and recording, specialised training, and long-term professional development; each fellowship is shaped by the recipient rather than a fixed programme. ELIGIBILITY IS NARROW AND GEOGRAPHIC: applicants must be current residents of South Australia and either final-year students or graduates within five years of a supported degree at Adelaide University, the University of Adelaide, Flinders University, or the University of South Australia. Honours students and graduates (up to five years after the final year of study) are eligible where honours was undertaken directly following the undergraduate degree. Masters and PhD candidates and graduates are not eligible unless they qualify through their undergraduate or honours study. Final-year students may apply provided the funded activity takes place after studies are completed and within the activity timeframe. Applications are assessed on artistic merit, alignment with career development, feasibility, commitment to learning, and level of ambition. The online application requires a CV (max two pages), an official academic transcript, a budget on the Helpmann template, a timeline, project confirmations, letters of support from an academic and an industry referee, and four to six images or one to two audio-visual work samples. An online information session runs 4 August 2026 at 6pm ACST, and the Program Manager, Toni Wills, takes online or in-person application chats (info@helpmannacademy.com.au). Applications opened 15 July 2026 and close 31 August 2026 at 11:59pm ACST, for activity occurring 1 January to 31 December 2027. Free to apply.

item.title: Liveline Fund: Round 1 (UK grassroots live music)
item.description:
Organisation: Liveline, delivered by Music Venue Trust with Save Our Scene and the Association of Independent Promoters

Location: United Kingdom. Guarantorship shows must be at Music Venue Alliance member venues; for a full tour at least 70 percent of dates must be at subscribed MVT venues. Regional focus includes the Highlands and Islands, West Wales and Northern Ireland.

Award: No fixed grant sizes published; every application is assessed case by case against a real budget rather than first come first served. The Guarantorship Scheme covers up to 80 percent of losses on a show or tour: if it breaks even nothing is paid, and if it turns a profit the promoter or venue keeps it. The other three funds cover venue hire, travel, accommodation, ferry and remote-access costs, or genre-specific safety, licensing and access costs. No application fee.

Duration: Round 1; applications close Tuesday 18 August 2026

Deadline: Closed 18 Aug 2026

Liveline is a national risk-sharing fund rebuilding grassroots touring, programming and local music scenes across the UK, delivered by Music Venue Trust with Save Our Scene and the Association of Independent Promoters, alongside the LIVE Trust and the industry's voluntary levy on stadium and arena tickets. The premise is that good shows are not happening because the downside risk is too high, so rather than a traditional subsidy it is an incentive-led model that only pays out when things go wrong. FOUR FUNDS: (1) GUARANTORSHIP SCHEME covers up to 80 percent of losses on an individual show or tour, for promoters, in-house bookers, artists or their representatives; break even and nothing is paid, turn a profit and you keep it. (2) LOCAL SCENE DEVELOPMENT FUND covers venue hire costs and local promoter training to build regular programming, for independent promoters or venues developing an in-house programme. (3) TOUR EXTENSION AND REGIONAL ACCESS FUND covers the long travel, fuel, accommodation and ferry costs that stop tours reaching remote parts of the UK, for promoters, agents, management and artists. (4) GENRE SPECIFIC SAFETY AND ACCESS FUND covers extra security, licensing and structural costs for genres and scenes that face additional barriers, for venues, promoters, artists or collectives. ELIGIBILITY: grassroots venues (Music Venue Alliance member venues), independent promoters including AIP members, in-house venue programmers, and artists, agents and teams building sustainable tours. Guarantorship shows must be at MVA subscribed venues, and for a full tour at least 70 percent of dates must be at subscribed MVT venues. TWO CATCHES WORTH KNOWING: tours must NOT already be announced, and Liveline funds a headline artist only once. Applications for Round 1 close Tuesday 18 August 2026. Start with the eligibility checker at livelinefund.uk, or contact info@livelinefund.uk.

This suits creators already working in video, social or short-form documentary who want to report accurately on a fast-moving legal area rather than guess at it. item.title: Alliance for Gender Equality in Europe: Strengthening Movements for Gender Equality (2026 call)
item.description:
Organisation: Alliance for Gender Equality in Europe (hosted by the Network of European Foundations)

Location: European Union, United Kingdom, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. All coalition partners must be based and operating in these countries.

Award: EUR 2,700,000 total across the call. Between EUR 225,000 and EUR 450,000 per grant over 3 years (EUR 75,000 to EUR 150,000 per year). Project support including salary and overhead costs; overheads capped at 20 percent. 6 to 12 coalitions expected to be funded. Free to apply.

Duration: 3 years, January 2027 to December 2029. Renewal possible at the end of the cycle subject to budget.

Deadline: Closed 07 Aug 2026

NOTE: this is a gender-equality movement-building fund rather than an arts or technology programme, and it is coalition-only (no individual applicants). Relevance to creative or tech practice runs through the narrative-change and digital-storytelling strand of the call. The Alliance for Gender Equality in Europe, a philanthropic initiative created in 2021 and hosted by the Network of European Foundations, is launching an open call under its forthcoming Strengthening Movements Fund. The Alliance is composed of the Bodossaki Foundation, Fondation BNP Paribas, Fondation CHANEL, Fondazione con il Sud, Fondation de France, Fondation RAJA-Danièle Marcovici, King Baudouin Foundation and L'Oréal Fund for Women; this particular fund is backed by all of those except Fondation BNP Paribas. OBJECTIVE: to foster collaboration and solidarity within European intersectional and grassroots movements so that they can collectively advance gender equality in Europe in the long term. The call follows a 2025 Alliance-commissioned mapping of European gender-equality movements (30 in-depth interviews plus contextual research) which found movements under-resourced because philanthropic funding frameworks are misaligned with their needs; the fund is designed to replace short-term reactive funding with proactive long-term support. OUTCOMES SOUGHT: community organising reinforced at local or national level; pan-European feminist collaborations and solidarity strengthened; alliances between gender equality and other social justice movements expanded; pro-gender-equality narratives and voices amplified in local, national, regional or digital spaces; policy debates informed by feminist and gender equality movements. ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE (non-exhaustive): national, regional or pan-European convenings and collaborative projects where groups co-create joint strategies; joint campaigns between feminist movements and allied movements (climate justice, anti-racism, LGBTQI+, disability rights); narrative-change training for grassroots groups covering framing, messaging, digital tools and digital storytelling; cross-border coalitions advocating EU institutions or national governments; facilitated virtual or in-person convenings to work through internal tensions and build trust; translating academic research on anti-gender efforts into movement strategies. ELIGIBILITY: collective proposals with at least 3 organisations per coalition (no maximum); legally registered non-profits (NGOs, civil society organisations, social enterprises, national or regional funds); based and operating in the target countries; small and medium grassroots organisations, defined by annual budget under EUR 450,000 (Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Sweden, UK) or under EUR 300,000 (Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Republic of Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Serbia). Intermediary organisations and networks are exempt from the budget thresholds but must apply in coalition with grassroots organisations, with the budget fairly distributed among all partners. Coalitions must be community-led (majority of leadership roles held by members of the community supported, and/or participatory approaches), work with marginalised women, transgender, non-binary and gender non-conforming people, use gender transformative approaches, and hold an intersectional perspective. Proposals must be completed in English. Each organisation may submit only one application, as lead or as partner. One organisation per coalition acts as lead, is the primary contact and is legally responsible for the grant; leads are invited to networking, peer-learning and capacity-strengthening activities. SCORING (100 points): relevance to the call objective 20; demonstrated track record in strengthening movements 20 (learnings valued as well as achievements); strong impact 25 (must contribute to at least one of the five outcomes, with clear measurement); ability to work collaboratively and inclusively with partners 20 (including fair budget repartition); quality and feasibility 15. PROCESS: two stages. Stage 1 opened 29 June 2026 and closes 7 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST, submitted in English via the online platform (a PDF of the form is downloadable for reference only). Pre-selection results by email 14 September 2026; stage 2 runs 16 September to 23 October 2026 and includes due-diligence contact from Alliance staff; final results by email in December 2026; grants start January 2027. The Alliance is piloting a participatory selection process for this call, with grant-making decisions made jointly by a committee of funders and non-funders holding equal decision-making power. Q&A webinars: 6 July 2026 at 14:00 CEST and 15 July 2026 at 10:00 CEST (registration in advance; both have passed). An updated FAQ is published on the call page.
